{"result":"# The Rust Programming Language and Memory Safety

Rust is a general-purpose language that emphasizes performance, type safety, concurrency, and memory safety [1]. Its syntax resembles C++, yet it guarantees memory safety without a garbage collector [2].

## Why Memory Safety Matters

Memory safety protects programs from bugs such as buffer overflows and dangling pointers [3]. Java achieves this partly through runtime checks on array bounds and pointer dereferences [3], while C, C++, and Fortran allow arbitrary pointer arithmetic without bounds checking [3].

## How Rust Enforces Safety

Rust shifts many of these guarantees into the compiler, so problematic code is rejected before it runs.

## Functional Influences

Rust draws on functional programming ideas such as immutability, algebraic data types, and pattern matching [1].

## Milestones

Graydon Hoare began Rust in 2006, and Mozilla Research sponsored it from 2009 [2]. The first public release came in 2010, and version 1.0 followed in 2015 [2].

## Conclusion

## How Rust Enforces Safety

Rust moves many of these guarantees into compile-time checks, so problematic code is rejected before it runs.

## Functional Influences

Rust draws on functional programming ideas such as immutability, algebraic data types, and pattern matching [1].

## Milestones

Graydon Hoare began Rust in 2006, and Mozilla Research sponsored it from 2009 [2]. Its first public release came in 2010, and version 1.0 followed in 2015 [2].

## Conclusion
